pitch:
# A minesweeper game

## 1. People and their journey
**Player** is the only role. They arrive at the board, see a fresh grid of hidden cells, a mine counter and a timer. They reveal and flag cells to clear every safe cell without hitting a mine, then see the win or loss and start a new game from the face button.

## 2. How it looks
The product looks like classic Windows Minesweeper: a grey titled desktop window on a teal desktop, with a menu bar, a sunken header panel and a sunken grid.

- **Desktop backdrop**: fills the browser page, flat teal (#008080); the window sits centred on it.
- **Window frame**: raised light grey (#C0C0C0) with a white top-left bevel and dark grey bottom-right bevel.
- **Title bar**: top of the window, dark blue (#000080) with white bold text "Minesweeper".
- **Menu bar**: under the title bar, light grey flat, with one entry "Game" in black. Highlights dark blue with white text while open.
- **Game menu**: drops below "Game", raised grey list: New, Beginner, Intermediate, Expert, Custom…, Marks (?), Best Times…, with a tick beside the current level and Marks when on.
- **Header panel**: top of the game area, sunken grey, holding counter, face and timer in a row.
- **Mine counter**: left of the header, sunken black box with three bright red (#FF0000) seven-segment digits showing mines minus flags; negative shows a minus sign.
- **Face button**: header centre, raised yellow smiley on grey square. Pressed: sunken. Cell held down: surprised "o" face. Won: sunglasses face. Lost: dead face with X eyes.
- **Timer**: right of the header, sunken black box with three red seven-segment digits counting seconds, capped at 999.
- **Grid**: below the header, sunken grey border containing square cells in rows and columns.
- **Hidden cell**: raised light grey square with white top-left and dark grey bottom-right bevel. While held down it looks sunken like a revealed empty cell.
- **Revealed empty cell**: flat pale grey (#C0C0C0) with thin darker grey outline, blank.
- **Number cell**: revealed look, bold number coloured 1 blue (#0000FF), 2 green (#008000), 3 red (#FF0000), 4 dark blue (#000080), 5 maroon (#800000), 6 teal (#008080), 7 black, 8 grey (#808080).
- **Flagged cell**: hidden-cell look with a red flag on a black base.
- **Question-marked cell**: hidden-cell look with a black "?" (only when Marks is on).
- **Mine cell**: on loss, unflagged mines show a black mine on the revealed look.
- **Exploded mine**: the mine the player hit, shown on a red (#FF0000) background.
- **Wrong flag**: on loss, a flag on a non-mine shows a mine with a red diagonal cross.
- **Won grid**: all remaining mines show flags.
- **Custom dialog**: small raised grey window titled "Custom Field" with Height, Width and Mines number fields and OK and Cancel buttons.
- **Best Times dialog**: small grey window listing fastest times for Beginner, Intermediate and Expert, with a Reset Scores and OK button.

## 3. How it is used
- Left-click a hidden cell: reveals it.
- Right-click a hidden cell, or long-press on touch: cycles hidden, flag, then question mark if Marks is on, else back to hidden.
- Click a revealed number cell: if the adjacent flags equal its number, reveals all other adjacent hidden unflagged cells (chord).
- Press both mouse buttons on a number, or middle-click: same chord.
- Press and hold on a cell: cell appears sunken and face turns surprised; releasing off the cell cancels.
- Click the face: starts a new game at the current level.
- Press F2: new game.
- Game menu, pick Beginner, Intermediate or Expert: starts a new game at that size.
- Game menu, Custom…: opens the dialog; OK validates and starts a new game.
- Game menu, Marks (?): toggles question marks.
- Game menu, Best Times…: shows the fastest times.
- Game menu, New: starts a new game.

## 4. Scope
One loop: pick a level, reveal and flag cells, win or lose, restart. Levels are Beginner, Intermediate, Expert and Custom. Single player, no accounts or online features. Best times are kept only on this device.

## 5. Things and their states
- **Cell**: holds mine or not, adjacent mine count. States: hidden, flagged, question-marked, revealed.
- **Board**: width, height, mine count, cells.
- **Game**: states ready (no mines placed yet), in progress, won, lost. Holds timer and flag count. First reveal moves ready to in progress; revealing a mine moves to lost; all safe cells revealed moves to won.

## 6. Rules
- Beginner is 9×9 with 10 mines.
- Intermediate is 16×16 with 40 mines.
- Expert is 30 columns × 16 rows with 99 mines.
- Custom height is 9 to 24, width 9 to 30, and mines 10 to (height−1)×(width−1); out-of-range values are clamped to the limit.
- Mines are placed on the first reveal, never on the clicked cell, so the first click is never a mine.
- The first click is also never adjacent to a mine in the standard layout only when space allows; otherwise only the clicked cell is safe.
- The timer starts on the first reveal and counts each second to 999.
- Each number shows the count of mines among the 8 neighbours.
- Revealing a zero cell automatically reveals all its neighbours, repeating through further zeros.
- Flood reveal skips flagged cells.
- Revealing a mine loses the game and stops the timer.
- Revealing every non-mine cell wins, stops the timer and flags all mines.
- A flagged or question-marked cell cannot be revealed by left-click; it is ignored.
- Revealed cells cannot be flagged; right-click is ignored.
- Flagging lowers the counter by one; removing raises it. Flags may exceed the mine count, so the counter may go negative.
- Chording with a mismatched flag count does nothing; if flags are wrong, chording can reveal a mine and lose.
- After win or loss, cells ignore clicks until a new game starts.
- Flags before the first reveal are allowed and do not start the timer.
- A winning time that beats the stored best for Beginner, Intermediate or Expert is saved on the device; Custom times are not saved.
- A new game resets timer to 000, counter to the mine count and face to smiling.
- The game can end only by a win, a loss, or the player starting a new game.
entities_block:
- **Game** (created by audience): [id: string, level: string, status: string, marks_enabled: boolean, elapsed_seconds: int, flag_count: int, mines_placed: boolean, boards: list of Board {id: string, width: int, height: int, mine_count: int}, cells: list of Cell {id: string, row: int, column: int, has_mine: boolean, adjacent_mine_count: int, state: string}, player_actions: list of PlayerAction {id: string, action_type: string, row: int, column: int, occurred_at: datetime}]
- **DifficultyLevel** (shown to audience: its records are loaded from the API): [id: string, name: string, height: int, width: int, mine_count: int]
action_protocol_block:
The rules the product enforces (plan the audience's side of them; the business's own back-office handling is out of view):
- [New game starts in ready state] (Game): Given the player has chosen a level When a new game is created Then the game status is ready, no mines are placed, elapsed_seconds is 0 and the mine counter equals the level's mine count
- [First reveal starts the game and timer] (Game): Given a game in ready state When the player reveals a cell Then mines are placed, the status becomes in progress and the timer starts
- [First click is never a mine] (Game): Given a game in ready state When the player first reveals a cell at position P Then the cell at P has no mine
- [First click neighbourhood safe when space allows] (Game): Given a game in ready state and enough space for a safe neighbourhood When the player first reveals cell P Then no neighbour of P and P itself contain a mine
- [First click safe only itself when space is short] (Game): Given a game in ready state where no safe neighbourhood fits the layout When the player first reveals cell P Then P has no mine while neighbours of P may contain mines
- [Flags before first reveal allowed without starting timer] (Game): Given a game in ready state When the player flags a cell Then the flag is recorded, the counter decreases by one, the status remains ready and the timer stays at 0
- [Revealing a mine loses the game] (Game): Given a game in progress When the player reveals a cell containing a mine Then the status becomes lost and the timer stops
- [Revealing all safe cells wins the game] (Game): Given a game in progress and all non-mine cells revealed When the last safe cell is revealed Then the status becomes won, the timer stops and every mine cell is flagged
- [Game ends only by win, loss or new game] (Game): Given a game in progress When any action other than revealing a mine, revealing the last safe cell or starting a new game occurs Then the status remains in progress
- [Cells ignore clicks after win or loss] (Game): Given a game in won or lost state When the player clicks or right-clicks any cell Then the board does not change
- [Timer counts seconds capped at 999] (Game): Given a game in progress with elapsed_seconds 998 When one more second passes and then another second passes Then elapsed_seconds becomes 999 and stays at 999
- [Mine counter equals mines minus flags] (Game): Given a board with 10 mines and 12 flags placed When the counter is read Then it shows -2
- [Flags may exceed mine count] (Game): Given a game with 10 mines and 10 flags placed When the player places an eleventh flag Then the flag is accepted and the counter shows -1
- [Left-click reveals hidden cell] (Game): Given a game in progress and a hidden cell When the player left-clicks it Then the cell state becomes revealed
- [Flagged or question-marked cell ignores left-click] (Game): Given a flagged or question-marked cell When the player left-clicks it Then the cell remains flagged or question-marked and is not revealed
- [Right-click cycles hidden, flag, question mark] (Game): Given a hidden cell and Marks on When the player right-clicks three times Then the cell goes flagged, then question-marked, then hidden
- [Right-click skips question mark when Marks off] (Game): Given a flagged cell and Marks off When the player right-clicks it Then the cell becomes hidden
- [Revealed cells cannot be flagged] (Game): Given a revealed cell When the player right-clicks it Then the cell remains revealed with no flag
- [Flagging and unflagging updates flag count] (Game): Given a hidden cell When the player flags it Then game flag_count increases by one and when the flag is removed flag_count decreases by one
- [Number cell counts neighbouring mines] (Game): Given a cell with 3 neighbouring mines When it is revealed Then its adjacent_mine_count is 3 and it displays 3
- [Zero cell floods neighbours] (Game): Given a cell with adjacent_mine_count 0 When it is revealed Then all its neighbours are revealed and each neighbour with count 0 reveals its own neighbours
- [Flood reveal skips flagged cells] (Game): Given a zero cell adjacent to a flagged cell When it is revealed Then the flagged cell stays flagged
- [Chord reveals neighbours when flags match number] (Game): Given a revealed cell showing 2 with exactly 2 adjacent flags When the player chords it Then all other adjacent hidden unflagged cells are revealed
- [Chord with mismatched flags does nothing] (Game): Given a revealed cell showing 2 with 1 adjacent flag When the player chords it Then no cell changes state
- [Wrong flags on chord can lose the game] (Game): Given a revealed cell showing 1 with one adjacent flag placed on a safe cell and a mine among the unflagged neighbours When the player chords it Then the mine is revealed and the status becomes lost
- [Chord via both mouse buttons or middle-click] (Game): Given a revealed number cell with matching adjacent flags When the player presses both mouse buttons on it or middle-clicks it Then the chord behaviour is applied
- [Press and hold cancels on release off cell] (Game): Given a hidden cell When the player presses on it and releases the pointer off that cell Then the cell stays hidden
- [Marks toggle controls question marks] (Game): Given Marks is off When the player toggles Marks on and then right-clicks a hidden cell twice Then the cell becomes question-marked and Marks is recorded as on
- [Beginner level dimensions] (DifficultyLevel): Given the player selects Beginner When a game is created Then the board is 9 by 9 with 10 mines
- [Intermediate level dimensions] (DifficultyLevel): Given the player selects Intermediate When a game is created Then the board is 16 by 16 with 40 mines
- [Expert level dimensions] (DifficultyLevel): Given the player selects Expert When a game is created Then the board has 30 columns, 16 rows and 99 mines
- [Custom height range with clamping] (DifficultyLevel): Given the Custom dialog When the player enters a height of 30 and confirms Then the height is clamped to 24
- [Custom width range with clamping] (DifficultyLevel): Given the Custom dialog When the player enters a width of 5 and confirms Then the width is clamped to 9
- [Custom mine range with clamping] (DifficultyLevel): Given a custom height of 9 and width of 9 When the player enters 100 mines and confirms Then the mine count is clamped to 64
- [New game at chosen level] (Game): Given a game in any state When the player clicks the face, presses F2 or selects New Then a new ready game is created at the current level
- [Custom level starts new game after validation] (Game): Given the Custom dialog with valid values When the player presses OK Then a new game starts with the custom height, width and mines
- [Face button reflects game outcome] (Game): Given a game that has been won When the state is displayed Then the face shows sunglasses
- [Exploded mine and wrong flags shown on loss] (Game): Given a game that has been lost When the board is displayed Then the exploded mine shows on red, unflagged mines show as mines and incorrect flags show a mine with a red cross
- [Number colours and counter digits] (Game): Given a revealed cell showing 3 When it is displayed Then the number is drawn in red #FF0000
- [Game menu tick marks current level and Marks] (Game): Given the current level is Expert and Marks is on When the Game menu is opened Then ticks appear beside Expert and Marks
intent_block:
- Product type: game
- Audience: players who want to play minesweeper for fun
- Goal: Let a player play a classic minesweeper round with clear rules, reveal and flag mechanics, and a win or loss outcome.
- Scope: A single-player minesweeper game consisting of a grid board, mine placement, cell reveal and flag interactions, and game state tracking through win or loss.
- The model must cover: board grid and cell state (hidden, revealed, flagged); mine layout and adjacency counts; game session state and outcome (in progress, won, lost); player moves (reveal, flag)
- Do NOT model: user accounts and login; leaderboards or online multiplayer; payments or monetisation; admin or back-office management of games
